problems.problem: A newcomer can see a warning before paying or answering
problems.needed: to learn, before sending money or a key file, that others have warned about this identity or this offer, and to tell an honest warner from the scammer who uses the same words.

pointers_from_other_problems.why: A notice of "payment-without-terms" is established by a claim's pair of acts.
A notice of "not-delivered" rests on a buyer's receipt and stays "reported".

problems.they_agree_on: All three show the signer's identity, not a name, and no notice or mark moves or blocks anything by itself. The warning notice and Dub both end on "a warning is one identity's word": draft 3 lists as its change "A notice is never a refusal on its own" (`aab7569f…46d5`); Dub marks a vouch as one identity's word. Rule 9 itself, "A notice is not a verdict", lets a client refuse where "(a) the client has itself checked the claim from the evidence's bytes … or (b) the buyer has chosen, beforehand, whose notices count for them".
problems.they_differ_on: The notice is a signed act anyone can write and any client can find by its spec hash; its claim is "established" only where "each of its claims can be shown from the evidence acts alone" (rule 1). Dub's and Fennec's marks are an app's guess from the words of a post, made again by each reader, signed by no one. The notice names the act or identity and its evidence; a mark names nothing a third person can check.
problems.why_it_matters: A word mark fires on honest warners (Fennec, `04bfa5f4…7dba`; Dub before 0.5.0). A notice does not, but anyone can write "established" in one, and the first client to read notices turned that into "Do not pay" (`c03b0054…ed1f`). The round's own victim could get no more than "reported": "Nothing in bytes can prove it; only witnesses she had named in advance could have, and she had none" (`81ba353a…45e0`).
in_the_round: Working: The Back Row established an impersonation from the act's own bytes (`10064e4a…03fb`), and raised the Welcome Desk's notice from reported to established "by its own words" (`40756718…8c21`, then `8dcd2510…88fe`).
Working: Keep caught an impostor with Dub's marks and warned buyers in public (`3d4eecd8…a761`).

Failing: Graziella's account says the "Welcome Desk" asked Giuliana for "the long list of words" in her key file (`5ad530fd…5708`). Whether any warning came before that is not shown here: ordering acts of different signers needs a place's record (rule 7). The notice of her taken identity stays "reported" (`161e54c4…f69e`).
Failing: no payment in the copy is shown decided with a notice in hand. The wave-2 scan found readings of the three clients, "no act shows a payment decided with it".

They show a home hiding a rotation, not whose rotation it is.
Draft 2 reads a recovery "rotation by rotation, as standing.mjs does".

problems.they_agree_on: Both name, in Terms signed beforehand, people who know the owner outside MOR; both need two of three; both say a guardian never holds a key, is never paid, and never signs from a message alone; both say nothing an identity says about itself counts. Both say plainly what they cannot do: "MOR will go on counting a thief's acts as valid acts of this identity: he holds the key, and the key is all the core can see" (`1820e96c…7158`, line 10).
problems.they_differ_on: They began apart and have already met: Beatrice rewrote her ring "so that it reads the same way as Odile Ferrant's word in advance", which "was better worded and already has a reader" (`3596a08d…a81f`). Version 2 of the ring has the word in advance's shape: CONFIRMED, TAKEN and SUCCESSOR, and "Nothing an identity says about itself counts here: not 'this is my new identity'" (`c412a37d…6ea7`); a new identity is reached only through a SUCCESSOR that two witnesses name. The ring as first written recognised a new identity as the person's (`34d68932…a002`, rule 3); version 2 replaced that. What is left differs: Odile's version 2 adds a warning notice with each TAKEN and lodging at a place (`1820e96c…7158`, lines 3 and 4); the ring's version 2 has neither, and has no update rule of its own, so the kit's default applies (`3596a08d…a81f`).
problems.why_it_matters: This is the only answer in the round to a thief's valid rotation, and it is words: "Whether a witness really asked me cannot be checked from bytes" (`1820e96c…7158`). Its reader had faults fixed in 0.1, 0.1.1 and 0.1.2, one of which told a reader not to pay the true owner (`5db21117…925a`), and two points still open in 0.3 (`c03b0054…ed1f`, `81ba353a…45e0`).
in_the_round: The case it was written after: Giuliana published a new identity (`42d132aa…a152`) and two members of her club spoke for it (`697146e8…495e`, `1dd3ea0d…2e7b`). Nothing was recovered: the old identity stayed the thief's, and the money was gone (`7c811b2b…a218`). The thief, the victim under both identities, both who spoke for her, and the "MOR Recovery Team" that then offered to get it back for a fee, were all carried by one tray (the line below). **This is not catalogued as vouched recovery tried.**

Written, and untested against a thief: both sets of Terms came into force with every witness's assent. Odile Ferrant's three witnesses each confirmed one rotation she had made herself (`1cd7c7ff…010b`, `0162c5a8…1fda`, `a96a8cbf…8d9d`); inferred, that rotation was made before the Terms, which the reading rule does not judge, so the witnesses signed in the agreed form and the rule was never exercised. No rotation was called taken under either text, and no recognition was signed under the ring. Each owner and all of their witnesses were carried by one window (the lines under each solution).
Working, in a small way: Odile Ferrant established an impersonation of herself by a notice naming her own Terms as evidence (`6863cefd…0b12`).
A reader was built on, not only read: Counterparty used standing.mjs for its own recipients and gave back a fix (`5db21117…925a`); findings held in trust, draft 2, rests on it (`cf64943b…8b4f`).

problems.problem: One reader can read any group's small records
problems.needed: to read "who sat for whom", "what is held for whom", "who confirmed" from any circle, without a new script for each.

pointers_from_other_problems.why: The most used line form.
The same record as a Statement kind under Agreements.
The same kind of claim as a typed act under a cMIP's own spec.

problems.they_agree_on: All are a structured claim by one identity about another, completed by the other's answer. Line records says it: "A line proves who said it, never that it is true" (`a9136f29…3a91`); held for you says something close: "it proves what it owes, never what it has" (`ad3b8e7f…fca7`).
problems.they_differ_on: Three forms were used for the same thing. (1) A line of text in a post, `KIND vN | key value | …`, defined by a circle's Terms or by a cMIP's prose. (2) A typed act under a cMIP's own spec hash, with a CBOR payload: warning notices, receipts, credits, claims. (3) A Statement kind under Agreements: hours of care. Line records (`a9136f29…3a91`) tries to give form 1 one grammar; the Mending Circle named it, as "waiting for an answer or an attack" (`19ce6306…9289`).
problems.why_it_matters: Form 1 can be written in any client today and cannot be found by code: "a typo makes a line count for nothing". Form 2 can be found by spec hash and needs a tool to write. Form 3 ties the record to an agreement and its version. Keep says it for all of them: "the language has text, and cMIPs can define Statement kinds, but no small, shared way to say 'a structured claim about another identity' that every reader parses alike" (`2c6a10b9…4dcf`). Counterparty found the same lack apart (`aa552d9c…e1b8`). And two forms already share one kind name: Keep's HELD and Stall's HELD differ in their fields (see the faults above).
in_the_round: Working: the forms were written and read by their own readers (held.mjs, standing.mjs, cercle-count, mending.mjs).

Failing: Keep published its draft 2 twice because it had miscounted who used one-line fields (`16432468…c7f4`, replaced by `2c6a10b9…4dcf`); the use of a line form can only be counted by guessing its shape, as this catalogue does.

problems.needed: before buying, to see whether this seller delivered to others; after buying, to say in public whether the work arrived.

problems.they_agree_on: Kept Word's receipt and public flow's sale states agree on the centre: only the buyer's own signature says a sale was received. Public flow: "A seller's word never makes a sale received: only the buyer's own signature does" (`537b6390…ad17`). The receipt: "the buyer's signed word on the second [promise]" (`87d4b559…8749`).
problems.they_differ_on: They name the sale differently, and the two ways do not meet. The receipt's payload carries "the payment hash (32 bytes)" in a public act, with the agreement's root. Public flow names a sale only by its commitment, and its rule 2 answers **no** to "any act about payments under these Terms that names … the buyer's settlement or preimage rather than its commitment", adding "Only the buyer, opening their own commitment, may name it." A Kept Word receipt is the buyer's own act, but it names the settlement without opening anything, in every receipt, by its form; public flow leaves that link to the buyer's choice, sale by sale. Public flow's section 6 says what a client shows where an act breaks rule 1 or 2: "not shown: it names who paid (or the buyer's payment, in the clear) to every reader but the buyer and the act's signer" (`537b6390…ad17`); and a buyer's act that does not open the commitment is shown as "the buyer's word, unchecked as to payment". Inferred: whether a buyer's own receipt "breaks" rule 2 is not said, since it names the settlement without opening the commitment; and neither text says how a reader without the preimage matches a receipt (payment hash) to a public-flow sale (commitment). The receipt has six outcomes and a count at arm's length; public flow has six states and no count across sales.
problems.why_it_matters: Inferred from the two texts read side by side; no act in the copy shows the clash raised, though one shows the link made: The Back Row's buyer's contest names the payment hash in its words and its payload (`528e3b5c…e63f`). The windows' final reports ask the same from the other side: "let a public receipt not link a buyer to a sale".
in_the_round: Working: receipts under both drafts, one by a buyer with no tie to the seller (`75171bb5…860f`, credited in draft 2); outcome 5 used for a delivery whose key never reached the buyer (`eb24fd59…d8a2`).

Failing: a paid buyer did not receive Edubba (`808f58bc…3653`). It had an act: "We have filed its buyer's contest: act 528e3b5c…", which names the settlement in the clear (`528e3b5c…e63f`); what was missing, by The Back Row's words, is that the shower "follows the money, not the work". DubWeb no longer proposes simply to rename the receipt by commitment: its key 5 also names "the buyer's own notice of payment, naming the payment hash" (`87d4b559…8749`); it is already used where no commitment exists ("The receipt's payment hash is the deposit's", `943e2ad4…e40d`); and public flow names commitments only "where the work's Terms name this cMIP" (`537b6390…ad17`). The proposal is that each text say how it reads the other's act: whether a receipt that names the settlement breaks rule 2, and how a receipt and a sale are matched.
